children: Senegal's dollar bonds fell to record lows on Tuesday after the government announced plans to restructure its debt as part of a provisionally agreed $2.2 billion, three-year International Monetary Fund agreement.

The country's dollar- and euro-denominated debt extended losses to leave them 3-4 cents and euro cents lower across the curve. Senegal's dollar bond due in 2031 dropped to 47.8 cents Tradeweb data showed, while the euro-denominated 2037 bond sank nearly 4 euro cents to 46.3.
